sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this writ petition under Section 528 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
seeking the quashing of FIR No. 225/2020, registered at Police Station Chanderi, District Ashoknagar, and all subsequent judicial proceedings arising therefrom.
Brief facts of the case are that the FIR arises from allegations that a property transaction of survey No. 238, area 0.064 hectare in Chanderi was fraudulently carried out.

The complainants alleged that the co-accused, including Chitransh Srivastava and Sandeep Srivastava, colluded to create a forged sale deed, falsely presenting an unknown person as the owner Neeraj Gupta and obtaining Rs. 11 lakh through deceit.
The petitioner was named in the FIR as a witness to the sale deed.
The FIR alleges offences under Sections 420, 467, 468, and 120B of IPC.
Counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is innocent and has no role in the alleged fraud.
The FIR is based on incorrect and fabricated facts.
The petitioner was merely a witness to the sale deed, and the main fraud was committed by the co-accused.
FIR registration was delayed, and no explanation NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7781 2 MCRC-7910-2026 for the delay has been given.
Therefore, the FIR and subsequent proceedings should be quashed.

Counsel for the State submitted that The FIR contains direct allegations against the petitioner, who Suresh Sharma Alias Suresh Kumar Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87077161/

sentences.text: Multiple statements and evidences collected during investigation point to the petitioner's involvement in the transaction.
Investigation has been completed and chargesheet filed, and quashing the FIR at this stage is not warranted.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
There are specific allegations against the petitioner, not merely technical or formal.

The petitioner's presence at the time of the alleged fraudulent transaction is supported by witness statements and his act of being signatory to the sale deed as a witness, prima facie proves his involvement.
In view of the direct allegations and the completed investigation, this Court finds no merit in the petitioner's contention for quashing the FIR.
Hence, the present petition is dismissed.
It is clarified that dismissal of this petition does not prevent the petitioner from raising his defense during trial.
(MILIND RAMESH PHADKE) JUDGE (aspr)
